What We Do

Full-Service Sports Medicine Revenue Cycle Management

Sports medicine billing combines orthopedic procedure coding, injection and aspiration billing, sports physical exam codes, occupational health coordination, and workers compensation routing. PMEX manages every element inside your existing sports medicine EHR workflow.

Musculoskeletal Procedure Coding

Arthroscopy, repair, and casting codes selected from the operative report by joint and procedure.

Joint Injection Billing

Arthrocentesis (20600 to 20611) coded by joint size with imaging guidance add-ons.

Sports Physical Coding

Pre-participation physicals coded with correct CPT and ICD-10 per payer benefit type.

PRP and Biologic Billing

Platelet-rich plasma and biologic injection billing managed with correct HCPCS codes.

Workers Comp Coordination

Work-related injuries routed to the correct WC carrier with first report documentation.

Imaging Guidance Billing

Ultrasound guidance (76942) billed alongside injections when documentation confirms use.

Sound Familiar?

Common Sports Medicine Billing Problems

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

Sports physical exam billed to medical insurance when it is a routine exam under the vision/wellness benefit.

PMEX confirms the exam type and routes sports physicals to the correct payer benefit category before billing.

PRP injection submitted without confirming payer coverage, generating a non-covered service denial.

PMEX verifies PRP coverage per payer before the injection is scheduled and manages prior authorization where required.

Joint injection billed without the ultrasound guidance add-on when guidance was used.

PMEX reviews every injection note for documented guidance and submits 76942 on every qualifying procedure.

Work-related sports injury filed to group health instead of the workers comp carrier.

PMEX identifies WC injuries at registration and routes all work-related claims to the correct WC carrier.

Arthroscopy coded at the wrong procedure level when the operative report supports a higher code.

PMEX reads every arthroscopy operative report and codes the procedure at the correct level per the documented anatomy.

Same-day E/M and procedure billed without modifier 25, payer bundles into the procedure.

PMEX applies modifier 25 to every E/M billed on the same day as a separately documented procedure.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in Sports Medicine Billing

Sports medicine practices lose 15 to 24 percent of revenue to PRP coverage denials, injection guidance omissions, and workers comp routing errors.

PATTERN 01

PRP Injection Denied as Non-Covered

Platelet-rich plasma injection administered for lateral epicondylitis. Claim submitted. Commercial payer denies: PRP is investigational under their coverage policy. No prior authorization was obtained. $680 denied with no appeal pathway.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX verifies PRP and biologic injection coverage per payer before the procedure is scheduled. Where coverage requires prior authorization or medical necessity documentation, PMEX manages the authorization process before the injection date.

PATTERN 02

Joint Injection Guidance Not Billed

Ultrasound-guided knee injection performed. 20611 (arthrocentesis, major joint) billed. 76942 (ultrasound guidance) not submitted. $65 in imaging guidance revenue not captured per injection. At 80 monthly guided injections, that is $5,200 monthly in unbilled add-on revenue.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX reviews every injection procedure note for documented ultrasound or fluoroscopic guidance and submits the correct imaging guidance add-on code alongside every injection where guidance is confirmed.

PATTERN 03

Work Injury Routed to Group Health

Athlete presents with a work-related shoulder injury. Front desk registers to the group health card. Group health denies as workers compensation injury. WC carrier never billed. Revenue lost and the patient receives a confusing bill.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX implements workers compensation identification at registration for all sports medicine practices, routing work-related injuries to the correct WC carrier with WC claim forms and first report documentation before any health insurance is billed.

Sports Medicine Billing Questions Answered

Sports physicals are billed using preventive medicine codes (99381 to 99395) when they are comprehensive evaluations, or with specific sports physical codes depending on the payer and whether the exam is for a school, team, or occupational requirement.

Coverage varies significantly by payer. Some commercial plans cover PRP for specific diagnoses such as lateral epicondylitis or knee osteoarthritis with prior authorization. Many plans still classify PRP as investigational. We verify coverage before the procedure.
